headline.definition: Equal-weight mean of (1 - AnchorHEC error / baseline error) across 36 camera-type conditions. The denominator is the baseline error in each individual condition; this is not a ratio of pooled errors.
headline.source_precision_note: Headline percentages were verified against full-precision canonical values. The records below preserve the two-decimal values printed in the paper; recomputation from rounded display values may differ slightly.

notes.simulation: Table II. Means over wrist subsets with an output. Two scenes per scene type, five trials per scene and wrist-pose budget, one top fixed camera (M=1), five images per fixed camera (Ne=5). Zhi and Schwertfeger does not use a 3DFM, so its values repeat across backbone panels.
notes.physical: Table IV. Two xArm6 acquisitions (room and tabletop), one fixed camera per acquisition. VGGT for JCR and AnchorHEC. Five wrist subsets, five images per fixed camera. Room Nw=25 subsets reuse all 25 poses; tabletop Nw=25 subsets are randomly sampled. No independent wrist-camera remounting was evaluated.
notes.status: complete means an estimate was returned for every subset, including any fallback estimates. It is not an accuracy or successful-registration guarantee. partial means only the indicated subsets returned estimates; their errors are conditional means. failed means no estimate was returned and both error fields are null.
notes.metrics: Translation error in centimetres and geodesic rotation error in degrees, against simulation ground truth or the physical calibration reference. Lower values are better.
notes.sf: SF is shared reconstruction frame placement applied by the AnchorHEC authors to the wrist transform and scale from JCR; JCR + SF is the fixed-camera comparison baseline.
